auth.scheme: OAuth 2 access token from POST /oauth/access_token; requests carry a versioned vendor media type in Accept (v1, JSON)

data_leaves_device: Not established. The fan reports a cloud endpoint (field 11) and a cloud identifier (field 9), which suggests it holds its own connection to the vendor service.

endpoints.name: Claim a device to the account
Firmware lookup
endpoints.returns: A token that resolves to a download URL for the image; needs a valid account and claim.

cloud.failure_mode: If the service goes away, account claim, off-LAN control, Alexa/Google linking, thermostat links and firmware downloads stop. The fan keeps working on the LAN: the app finds it by mDNS and drives it over 31415 with no account. One review reports schedules not firing during a cloud outage. Whether schedules depend on the cloud or that was a coincidence is not established.
cloud.notes: Endpoint shapes are from the vendor app (reported), recorded as evidence of the dependency. They are not a control surface and are not needed for anything this spec documents.

comfort_set_enabled.description: Turn Auto Comfort on or off.

comfort_set_heat_assist.description: Turn Heat Assist on or off (gently push warm air down when the room is well below the ideal temperature).

comfort_set_heat_assist_speed.description: Set the speed Heat Assist runs at.
comfort_set_heat_assist_speed.notes: Commit field 61, varint. Bounds are Home Assistant's (1-7); aiobafi6 does not check them.

comfort_set_ideal_temperature.example_notes: Rendered with temperature = 23.5 C, raw 2350, varint ae 12.
comfort_set_ideal_temperature.notes: Commit field 48, int32 varint in hundredths of a degree Celsius, whatever unit the app displays. Home Assistant turns Auto Comfort on first if it is off. The app's allowed range is not established; stay within ordinary room temperatures.

temperature.description: Ideal temperature in degrees Celsius; raw = round(temperature / 0.01).

comfort_set_max_speed.description: Set the highest speed Auto Comfort may choose (7 = no maximum).
comfort_set_max_speed.notes: Commit field 51, varint. aiobafi6 allows 0-7; Home Assistant offers 1-7.

comfort_set_min_speed.description: Set the lowest speed Auto Comfort may choose (0 = no minimum).
comfort_set_min_speed.notes: Commit field 50, varint. aiobafi6 allows 0-7; Home Assistant offers 0-6.

fan_set_eco.description: Turn Eco mode on or off (Haiku fans).
fan_set_eco.notes: Commit field 65, varint 0/1. Present when capability flag 14 is set (oogje).

fan_set_mode.description: Set the fan's power mode: off, on (manual speed) or Auto.
fan_set_mode.example_notes: Rendered with mode = 2 (auto). Off is ... d8 02 00 c0, on is ... d8 02 01 c0.
fan_set_mode.notes: Commit field 43, varint. Auto hands speed to Auto Comfort and motion sensing.

mode.description: 0 off, 1 on at the stored speed, 2 Auto.

fan_set_motion_sense.description: Let the fan's Auto mode respond to motion.

fan_set_motion_timeout.description: How long the fan keeps running after the last motion.
fan_set_motion_timeout.notes: Commit field 53, varint seconds. Bounds are Home Assistant's (1 min to 1 day); the app's own range is not established.

fan_set_return_to_auto.description: After a manual change, return the fan to Auto once a timeout passes.

fan_set_return_to_auto_timeout.description: How long after a manual change the fan returns to Auto.
fan_set_return_to_auto_timeout.notes: Commit field 55, varint seconds. Bounds are Home Assistant's (1 min to 12 h).

fan_set_reverse.description: Run the fan in reverse (updraft) or forward (downdraft).
fan_set_reverse.notes: Commit field 44, varint 0/1. The vendor app offers Reverse but advises against it, recommending a slow forward speed in winter instead.

fan_set_speed.description: Set the fan speed on the app's 1-7 scale; 0 stops rotation.
fan_set_speed.notes: Commit field 46, varint. If fan_mode is not 1 (on), commit fan_mode = 1 first, as Home Assistant does. aiobafi6 rejects anything outside 0-7 and so should a client: these are the only speeds the vendor app offers.

speed.description: Speed step. 1 is slowest and 7 fastest; 0 stops rotation.

fan_set_whoosh.description: Turn Whoosh on or off (speed varies around the current setting to feel like a breeze).

light_set_brightness.description: Set light brightness as a percentage.
light_set_brightness.notes: Commit field 69, varint 0-100. 0 turns the light off (oogje). Field 70 carries the same value as 0-16 steps.

light_set_color_preset.description: Pick one of the vendor app's named colour presets (Soft White, Bright White, and so on).
light_set_color_preset.example_notes: Rendered with kelvin = 3000 (Soft White), varint b8 17.
light_set_color_preset.notes: The same commit as light_set_color_temperature (field 71), limited to the app's preset table. The app hides presets outside the light's reported range (fields 78 and 79), and so should a client.

light_set_color_temperature.description: Set the light's colour temperature in kelvin.
light_set_color_temperature.example_notes: Rendered with kelvin = 4000 (Bright White), varint a0 1f.
light_set_color_temperature.notes: Commit field 71, varint kelvin (NOT mireds). Keep within the light's own range, fields 78 (warmest) to 79 (coolest). The vendor app offers only the preset values in protocol_details.baf_i6_api.light_color_presets.

light_set_dim_to_warm.description: Turn dim-to-warm on or off (the light warms as it dims).

light_set_mode.description: Set the light's mode: off, on or Auto.
light_set_mode.notes: Commit field 68, varint. On a fan with both an uplight and a downlight, field 82 picks which light this acts on (oogje, hypothesis).

light_set_motion_timeout.description: How long the light stays on after the last motion in Auto.
light_set_motion_timeout.notes: Commit field 73, varint seconds. Bounds are Home Assistant's (1 min to 1 day).

light_set_return_to_auto.description: After a manual change, return the light to Auto once a timeout passes.

light_set_return_to_auto_timeout.description: How long after a manual change the light returns to Auto.
light_set_return_to_auto_timeout.notes: Commit field 75, varint seconds. Bounds are Home Assistant's (1 min to 12 h).

query_all.description: Ask for every property. The fan answers with one or more PropertySet frames.
query_all.notes: Query group 0: outer field 2, envelope field 3, query field 1 = 0.

query_group.notes: Query field 1 = group. The frame is c0 12 04 1a 02 08 <group> c0 for any group below 128.

values.3: firmware, clock and API (the vendor app's timer query)

txt_match.description: Read by both aiobafi6 (discovery.py) and the vendor app, which defaults it to 0 when absent. aiobafi6 ignores services whose value is below 4. Occupancy readings need 5 or later.
The vendor app's model table (reported). The app falls back to "i6" when the key is missing.

methods.notes: aiobafi6 keys services by TXT uuid rather than by instance name, because a renamed fan's old record lingers until its TTL expires. It also checks after connecting that the fan's own field-10 value matches, and drops the connection if it does not. The vendor app also browses `_http._tcp`, for a reason not established. Do not treat `_http._tcp` as a fan signal.
Setup-time discovery only: the vendor app's Add Product flow scans for this service (reported). Use it to find a fan that is not yet on Wi-Fi. Day-to-day control is the mDNS/TCP path above.

mac_prefixes.notes: Delta Electronics' block (IEEE registry). It appears, with the NIC half zeroed, in the example fan configuration of the homebridge-i6-bigassfans README. That suggests the smart board's Wi-Fi module comes from Delta Electronics, but no unit has been seen by this project. The block belongs to a large electronics maker and says nothing about the product on its own.

mdns_txt_match.description: The fan publishes its protocol API version under a TXT key with a space in it. That key is the distinctive part of this record set; `_api._tcp` is a generic-sounding type another product could use.

Model strings the vendor app recognises (i6, es6, Haiku H/I Series, Haiku L Series, Haiku Light, Haiku Switch, and the Turbo6, Mammoth, Bison and Speakeasy fans). Home Assistant matches only `haiku*` and `i6*`, so its matcher misses es6.

identification.notes: Primary identity is the mDNS record. The BLE service UUID is what the vendor app filters its scan on when adding a product, so it also identifies a fan that is not yet on Wi-Fi. Whether a provisioned fan keeps advertising it has not been established. The `uuid` TXT value equals the fan's own reported service UUID (property field 10), and it is the stable identity; the display name is the TXT `name`.

device.name: Big Ass Fans i6 / es6 / Haiku (firmware 3.x)
device.notes:
Big Ass Fans' residential line (Haiku H/I and L series, i6, es6) and its Haiku lights and wall controls, on firmware 3.x. In April 2022 Big Ass Fans moved the Haiku line to the protocol the i6 already spoke, retired the old Haiku (SenseME) app, and the legacy ASCII protocol stopped answering on those fans. Integrations built on it (aiosenseme, Hubitat drivers) broke. The Big Ass Fans app is the vendor client for this generation.
LOCAL AND ACCOUNT-FREE. The fan announces itself as `_api._tcp` over mDNS and accepts a plain TCP connection on port 31415 (no TLS, no key, no login). Every message in either direction is one protobuf message in a SLIP frame (0xc0 ... 0xc0, with 0xc0 and 0xdb escaped). A client sends two kinds of message: a QUERY for a group of properties, and a COMMIT that sets one property. The fan answers queries with property sets, and PUSHES a property set to connected clients whenever something changes. That includes the fan confirming a commit: there is no separate acknowledgement. The field-level map is in protocol_details.baf_i6_api; the exact bytes of every command are in its example_body.
WHAT A CLIENT CAN DO. Everything the vendor app exposes for the fan: power and Auto (fan mode off/on/auto), speed 1-7, Reverse, Whoosh, Eco (Haiku), Auto Comfort (on/off, ideal temperature in hundredths of a degree Celsius, minimum and maximum speed), Heat Assist (on/off and its own speed), motion sensing, and return-to-Auto timeouts. For the light: mode off/on/auto, brightness 0-100 %, colour temperature (the app's presets run from Warm 2200 K to Daylight 6500 K, including Soft White 3000 K and Bright White 4000 K, filtered to what the light kit reports it can do), and dim-to-warm. Readings: temperature, humidity, fan RPM, and two occupancy flags (firmware 3.1, API version 5 and later). Schedules and sleep mode exist on the device, but their wire format is unknown.
WHERE THE SENSORS ARE. On some models the temperature and humidity come from the Bluetooth remote or wall control, not the fan (Home Assistant's documentation; oogje says so for the i6). When the fan loses its remote, those readings and Auto Comfort stop updating while the fan itself stays reachable.
CLOUD. api.bigassfans.com handles account claim, off-LAN control, voice assistants, thermostat links and firmware downloads. LAN control does not touch it. See `cloud`.
BLE. The fan also carries a vendor BLE service. The app uses it to find unprovisioned fans and to push Wi-Fi credentials, and it can send the same SLIP-framed protobuf messages over it when the LAN path is unavailable (reported, from the app). Only the UUIDs and chunking are recorded here, in setup.methods[0].ble and protocol_details. Earlier notes said three vendor "BLE UUIDs" belonged to the wall-remote pairing. That was wrong: those three strings are thermostat-integration identifiers in the app, not GATT UUIDs, and they are left out on purpose.

openness.notes: Big Ass Fans publishes no local API. The protocol was worked out by the community: aiobafi6 (jfroy, with bdraco suggesting protobuf) and the homebridge plugin by oogje. Home Assistant has shipped aiobafi6 in its `baf` integration since 2022.6, so this protocol runs in production. The schema lives only in aiobafi6's hobbyist .proto; nothing here comes from a vendor document. Current smart boards also ship with a Matter QR sticker (vendor board-replacement instructions), so Matter is a second, standard local path on newer units. This spec does not cover it.

pairing.notes: Nothing pairs on the control path. The TCP socket on 31415 takes any LAN client with no key, token or handshake (aiobafi6, oogje, and the vendor app's plain socket). The BLE setup channel is also used without a bond (reported). The Bluetooth remote and wall control are a separate, device-to-device pairing and are not part of this protocol. Press any remote button near the fan to pair. Hold fan power and fan minus until the remote's LEDs flash to clear the remote's pairings. The fan plays a jingle when a remote pairs (vendor support pages, i6 manual).

credentials.notes: Nothing is issued to a LAN client. Port 31415 is unauthenticated, so anything on the LAN can drive the fan. How the passphrase is protected on the BLE channel is not established: the channel is unbonded, and no encryption layer was seen above the SLIP frames.
stored_on_device: Fan name, room/group membership and every setting in the property table

factory_reset.description: The i6 manual documents two routes: one from the paired remote, and one by cycling power at the wall. Both end with the fan's LED turning green. The Haiku board instructions only point at the support site, so applying these to Haiku and es6 is unestablished. The app also refers to a network-only reset ("reset its network settings") without giving its procedure here.
factory_reset.effect: Erases all settings, including the fan's name and its Wi-Fi network (i6 manual). The fan leaves the LAN and must be added again with the app. Whether a Bluetooth remote's pairing survives is not stated.

procedures.basis: Big Ass Fans i6 operation and maintenance manual, troubleshooting section.
procedures.indicator: The fan beeps and its LED blinks slowly; the reset is complete when the LED blinks green.
procedures.name: Remote: hold fan power, then press fan minus

steps.action: Press and hold the fan power button on the paired remote for 5 seconds.
steps.expect: The remote LEDs start blinking and the fan beeps.

steps.action: Press the fan minus button on the remote.
steps.expect: The fan beeps and its LED indicator blinks slowly for a few moments, then blinks green.

procedures.basis: Big Ass Fans i6 operation and maintenance manual, troubleshooting section (reset without the remote).
procedures.indicator: The fan's LED indicator turns green.
procedures.name: Wall switch or breaker: four off/on cycles

steps.action: Turn the fan's wall switch or breaker off and wait about 5 seconds.
Turn it back on and wait about 5 seconds.
Repeat the off/on cycle three more times, four cycles in all.
steps.expect: The fan's LED indicator turns green: the reset is complete.

ble.protocol: Vendor BLE channel carrying the same SLIP-framed protobuf messages as TCP 31415

methods.description: The only onboarding route established for 2023-and-later units, and the one the vendor documents. The app finds the fan by its vendor BLE service, confirms it with an audible and visual Identify, sends the home network credentials, and then finds the fan again on the LAN. The app writes SLIP-framed protobuf to the write characteristic in 20-byte pieces and reads replies from notifications. It requests a 250-byte MTU and calls no bonding API (reported, from the app).
methods.name: Big Ass Fans app: find the fan over Bluetooth, send it Wi-Fi

steps.action: Install the fan and power it at the wall switch or breaker.
steps.expect: The fan beeps once on power-up, unless beeps have been turned off in the app.

steps.action: In the Big Ass Fans app choose Add Product. The app scans for devices advertising service e0fc1000-1fb1-4168-96df-b3f057a86e01 and lists what it finds.
Press Identify on the fan the app offers.
steps.expect: The chosen fan beeps and flashes its LEDs.

steps.action: Pick the home network and enter its passphrase. The app sends it to the fan over the BLE channel.
steps.expect: The app reports the fan connected to the network.

steps.action: Browse _api._tcp.local., match the TXT uuid, and open TCP 31415.
steps.expect: A query_all answered with the fan's properties. Field 10 equals the TXT uuid.

causes: Android 12 and later Bluetooth/location permissions. A reviewer (an Android developer) could only add the fan from an iPhone, after which Android control worked.
The fan is already on a network. A provisioned fan does not re-enter setup until its network settings are reset (the app's own advice).
troubleshooting.symptom: The app cannot find the fan over Bluetooth on Android.

causes: The phone is on a VPN. The app detects VPNs and asks for them to be turned off, because mDNS and the LAN socket do not cross one.
The phone changed networks during setup. One reviewer had to turn phone Wi-Fi off while the fan joined.
The router blocks multicast between clients (AP or client isolation), so _api._tcp never arrives.
troubleshooting.symptom: The fan joins, then the app says it could not find the device on the network.

causes: The passphrase contains a double quote, which the product does not support (the app warns about this).
troubleshooting.symptom: The fan will not accept the Wi-Fi password.

setup.notes: A factory-fresh fan has to be put on Wi-Fi by the Big Ass Fans app. The vendor help page describes the flow: Add Product, the app searches over Bluetooth, Identify makes the chosen fan beep and flash, then Wi-Fi is entered and the fan is named. The app's BLE channel and its framing are known (reported). The Wi-Fi credential message itself has not been established, so this cannot yet be done without the app. Whether the app lets onboarding finish without signing in to a Big Ass Fans account is also not established. The app has a cloud claim step, and a review describes backing out of sign-up to reach local devices. Once the fan is on the LAN, nothing on the control path needs an account. The app also offers a "Wi-Fi (before 2023)" route for Haiku L fans bought before 2023, which join over Wi-Fi rather than Bluetooth. That route's mechanism is not documented here.

rejoin.notes: The app's advice for reconnecting a product is to reset its network settings and then Add Product again. No in-place path to change Wi-Fi over the LAN socket is known. The only reset documented for the i6 clears everything, name included. Identity survives in the sense that field 10 and the TXT uuid are the fan's own; whether they change on reset is not established.

testing.notes: No Big Ass Fans hardware has been driven from this file by this project, and the research store holds no capture of real traffic. The byte sequences are aiobafi6's serializer, reproduced with an independent standard-library encoder (varint, length-delimited fields, RFC 1055 SLIP). The two agree on every example_body and test vector here. The transport (plain TCP to 31415, no TLS), the SLIP escapes, the _api._tcp browse, the BLE channel and the colour-preset table were cross-checked statically against the vendor Android app v3.3.4 and 3.4.0. Checking against real hardware should start with three things: whether the fan accepts more than one property per commit, the humidity scaling (aiobafi6 and oogje disagree), and whether the fan serves several TCP clients at once.

entities.name: Fan
entities.notes: Seven speeds. fan_mode 2 (Auto) counts as neither on nor off here; the Fan Mode select shows it. To set a speed from any mode, send fan_set_mode 1 and then fan_set_speed, as Home Assistant does.

entities.name: Reverse
entities.notes: The vendor app offers this but recommends never reversing.

entities.name: Eco Mode
entities.notes: Haiku fans per oogje. Capability flag 14 is the run-time test.

entities.name: Auto Comfort
entities.notes: Both temperatures are hundredths of a degree Celsius on the wire (the entity-level scale). Offer this only when capability flags 1 and 3 are both set, as Home Assistant does. On some models the room temperature comes from the remote, so this entity can go stale while the fan stays reachable. temp_step is a UI choice, not a device resolution. The app shows whole degrees; the wire carries hundredths.

entities.name: Light
entities.notes: Brightness is a percentage, 0-100, not 0-255. A fan's light kit is optional: draw this only when capability flag 4 (downlight) or the uplight flag is set. On an uplight-only fan the downlight flag is unset, yet these fields still drive the uplight (aiobafi6).

entities.name: Light Colour
entities.notes: The vendor app's picker. Hide options outside the light's reported range (fields 78 to 79). A light whose range is two presets wide shows only Soft White and Bright White, as in the app's store screenshots.

entities.name: Temperature
entities.notes: Hundredths of a degree Celsius on the wire. Pushed on change. On some models it comes from the remote.

entities.name: Humidity
entities.notes: Whole percent per aiobafi6, which Home Assistant ships; a value outside 0-100 means no sensor. oogje divides the raw value by 100, so the scaling is unresolved until someone reads a real unit.

entities.name: Fan Speed RPM
entities.notes: Not pushed on change; refreshed only by a query.

entities.name: Fan Occupancy
entities.notes: API version 5 or later (firmware 3.1). Clears about 4.5-5 minutes after the last motion.

entities.name: Light Occupancy
entities.notes: API version 5 or later. Clears about 9.5 minutes after the last motion.

evidence.app_static_analysis: A targeted check of the vendor app, not a full analysis. It confirms that the app browses `_api._tcp` (and `_http._tcp`) with Android NSD, reads the TXT keys name, uuid, model and "api version", and opens a plain TCP socket to port 31415 with a 10 s connect timeout and keepalive. Its frame encoder and decoder are SLIP (0xc0 delimiters, 0xdb 0xdc / 0xdb 0xdd escapes). Its query message takes values 0-8, and it sends 0 for a full refresh and 3 on a timer. It carries the colour-preset table and filters it by the light's warmest and coolest values. It scans BLE for service e0fc1000-..., writes 20-byte chunks to e0fc1003-..., takes notifications on e0fc1004-..., and requests a 250-byte MTU. It uploads firmware over HTTP to port 31416. An earlier note in the research store said the app speaks only legacy UDP ASCII. That is wrong for this generation: the ASCII vocabulary is also present, for the legacy fans, but the 3.x path is the one above.

evidence.documentation_review: Manuals give the reset and remote-pairing procedures. The support pages give the onboarding sequence. No FCC ID is printed in the manuals held, and no Big Ass Fans / Delta T grantee was found on fccid.co.
open_questions: Does the fan accept more than one property in a single commit?
Humidity scaling: whole percent (aiobafi6) or hundredths (oogje)?
How many simultaneous TCP clients does the fan serve, and does every connection get pushes?
Which capability sub-field is the uplight: 6 (aiobafi6) or 11 (oogje)?
What protobuf message carries the Wi-Fi SSID and passphrase over the BLE channel, and is anything encrypted above the SLIP layer?
What do query groups 7 and 8 return?
What is the schedule message format (query group 5, query_result field 3), and do schedules fire with the cloud unreachable?
Does a provisioned fan keep advertising its BLE service?
Does the i6 manual's reset apply unchanged to es6 and Haiku, and is there a network-only reset?

dfu_mode.notes: Not established. The fan's appearance and mDNS record during an update have not been observed.

enter.notes: The running fan receives the image from the phone on an HTTP server at TCP 31416 (reported, from the app). The request path and body format are deliberately left out. Whether a protobuf message prepares the fan first is not established; an app error named "preparation failed" suggests one.

image.format: Not established. No image is held.
image.notes: The app fetches a token from the cloud firmware lookup, downloads the image, and uploads it to the fan over the LAN (reported, from the app). The app carries two upload generations. Download URLs are token-gated, so a replacement client cannot fetch images without an account.

dfu.notes: Firmware update is the one path here that can leave a fan unusable, and no client other than the vendor app should attempt it. It is recorded so a reader knows port 31416 exists and what it is for.

recovery.notes: Reviews report fans that stopped working after the 3.0 update until vendor support talked the owner through recovery, and a light kit that vanished after a 2026 update. The app can also downgrade a Haiku to the legacy firmware (support-directed only), which factory resets the fan and needs the old Haiku app to re-add it.

initialization.description: Once per connection, straight after the TCP connect: ask for every property. The reply is the client's starting state, and pushes keep it current from then on. A client that also wants the vendor app's keepalive can repeat query_group with group 3 on a timer.

covers: Fan mode, speed, direction, Whoosh, Eco
Auto Comfort ideal temperature, minimum and maximum speed, Heat Assist
Motion sensing and return-to-Auto settings for fan and light
Light mode, brightness, colour temperature, dim-to-warm
Temperature, humidity, RPM and occupancy readings, pushed on change
not_covered: Initial Wi-Fi onboarding (the app's BLE credential message is not documented)
Off-LAN control, voice assistants and thermostat links
Schedules and sleep mode (wire format unknown)
local_access.notes: Matter is a second local route on units whose smart board carries a Matter QR code. This spec does not cover it.
local_access.summary: Fully local as shipped. mDNS finds the fan, a plain TCP socket controls it, and state is pushed. There is no account, token or cloud relay on the path, and the fan keeps running its local surface with the internet down.

PropertySet.description: What the fan sends: the outer message, then envelope field 4 (query_result), holding one or more property sets. The fields below are the ones the entities bind, named as in protocol_details.baf_i6_api. Units and scaling are for the decoded value.

fields.description: Field 87, varint. Whole percent per aiobafi6; oogje divides by 100 (unresolved).
fields.name: humidity

parse_rules: Split the byte stream on 0xc0, skip empty frames, then un-escape db dc -> c0 and db dd -> db.
Decode the protobuf message: outer field 2 -> envelope field 4 -> repeated field 2 property sets.
Merge every property set into one running copy, field by field, later values winning. A push carries only what changed.
Ignore field numbers you do not know, and do not merge them.
Treat fields 4, 5, 64 and stats (156) as volatile. They change without anything happening, so leave them out of change detection (aiobafi6).

ble_channel.notes: Reported, from the vendor app, which also reads Model Number and Serial Number from the standard Device Information service. The app uses this channel for Add Product and, when it has no LAN path to a fan, to send the same protobuf messages. The Wi-Fi credential message is not established. The app's code names further slots on the same UUID base (0x1001, 0x1002, 0x1100-0x1102); their roles are unknown.
ble_channel.notify: e0fc1004-1fb1-4168-96df-b3f057a86e01 (notifications carry SLIP frames; enable the 0x2902 descriptor)
ble_channel.write: e0fc1003-1fb1-4168-96df-b3f057a86e01 (write with response, 20-byte pieces of a SLIP frame)

capability_flags.description: Boolean sub-fields of field 17. Prefer these over the model table when deciding which controls to draw. The two open projects disagree on sub-field 6.

flags.1: Temperature sensor (oogje). aiobafi6 calls it comfort flag 1; Home Assistant offers Auto Comfort only when 1 and 3 are both set.
flags.3: Occupancy sensor (oogje). aiobafi6 calls it comfort flag 3.
flags.4: Downlight (oogje); has-light (aiobafi6). On an uplight-only fan it is unset, yet the light fields still drive the uplight.
flags.6: CONFLICT: colour-temperature control (oogje) or has-uplight (aiobafi6, seen on Haiku H/I with an uplight module).

commit_rules: Put one property in each commit. aiobafi6 always does and says it is unknown whether the firmware accepts more than one per commit.
Do not update local state on send. Wait for the fan to push the new value back.

Speed and fan mode are separate properties. To run the fan at a chosen speed, Home Assistant commits fan_mode = 1 (on) when the mode is anything else, then commits speed. Whether a speed commit alone takes the fan out of Auto is not established.

Committing speed 0 stops rotation, and committing light brightness 0 turns the light off (oogje). oogje first commits 1 and then 0, so that turning on again later restores a low level instead of the previous one; that is a HomeKit workaround, not a protocol rule.

rules: Connect to the address and port from the _api._tcp record. The vendor app uses a 10 s connect timeout and turns on TCP keepalive (reported); aiobafi6 and oogje also set keepalive.
Send query_all right after connecting. The fan answers with its whole property set, spread over one or more frames.
Keep the socket open. The fan pushes a property set on every change, which is how commits are confirmed (aiobafi6 device.py).

Re-query now and then for values the fan does not push, such as RPM and clock. aiobafi6 defaults to every 60 s; Home Assistant uses 300 s. The vendor app repeats query group 3 on a timer, about every 15 s according to oogje.

Expect the fan to drop the connection occasionally (oogje). Reconnect, and retry a command that was sent at the moment of the drop: oogje suggests after about 2 s. aiobafi6 waits 30 s between connect attempts.
Whether the fan accepts several clients at once is not documented. Home Assistant and the vendor app are routinely used together, which suggests it does.

encoding.signed: Fields are int32. A negative value (a temperature below 0 C) is sign-extended to a 10-byte varint, per protobuf int32 rules.
encoding.unknown_fields: The fan sends many fields no client names. Skip them. aiobafi6 discards them before merging, because merging would treat unknown fields as repeated and grow without bound.
encoding.varint: Base-128, least-significant 7-bit group first, high bit set on every byte but the last. Every number and boolean on this protocol is a varint (wire type 0); strings and nested messages are length-delimited (wire type 2).

escapes: 0xc0 inside a message is sent as 0xdb 0xdc
0xdb inside a message is sent as 0xdb 0xdd
framing.notes: No length prefix and no checksum: the delimiters are the only boundaries. A TCP read can hold part of a frame or several frames. aiobafi6 refuses an empty frame (c0 c0) and drops the connection. The vendor app's decoder skips it instead (reported), so skip it. The 4096-byte ceiling is aiobafi6's receive-buffer limit ("no message is ever expected to be larger"), not a documented maximum. The same framing crosses the BLE channel, chunked into 20-byte writes (reported).
framing.scheme: RFC 1055 SLIP around each protobuf message

light_color_presets.description: The vendor app's colour picker offers these presets, dropping any outside the range the light reports in fields 78 (warmest) and 79 (coolest). Picking one commits field 71 with the Kelvin value. Reported, from the app.

commit.field_3: property set (length-delimited): a property-set message carrying the field(s) to change.

message_tree.description: Every frame, in both directions, is the same outer message. Only one path through it is used per frame. Field numbers from aiobafi6's .proto, cross-checked against oogje's hand-built frames. Names are ours.

envelope.field_2: commit (length-delimited). Client to fan: set properties.
envelope.field_3: query (length-delimited). Client to fan: ask for a property group.
envelope.field_4: query_result (length-delimited). Fan to client: answers and pushes.

outer.field_2: envelope (length-delimited). The only field of the outer message.

query_result.field_2: property set (length-delimited, repeated). Merge each one into the client's copy, later values winning.
query_result.field_3: schedule (length-delimited, repeated). Returned for query group 5. Contents unknown.

properties.name: name
properties.notes: User-assigned device name.

properties.name: model
properties.notes: Same strings as the TXT model record.

properties.name: local_time
properties.notes: ISO 8601 local time. Changes every read; exclude it from change detection.

properties.name: utc_time
properties.notes: ISO 8601 UTC time. Volatile, as field 4.

properties.name: firmware_version
properties.notes: oogje has seen it arrive zero-length.

properties.name: service_uuid
properties.notes: Equals the TXT uuid on _api._tcp. aiobafi6 refuses a connection whose value does not match the service it resolved.

properties.name: cloud_endpoint
properties.notes: oogje sees the vendor cloud's API host here.

properties.name: api_version
properties.notes: Decimal string. aiobafi6 needs 4 or later; occupancy fields need 5 or later (firmware 3.1).

properties.name: firmware_detail
properties.notes: Sub-fields: 2 version string, 3 bootloader version, 4 MAC (aiobafi6). oogje reads sub-field 1 as the component (0 host, 1 Wi-Fi, 2 light, 3 motor), so the field may repeat once per component.

properties.name: capabilities
properties.notes: Boolean sub-fields. See capability_flags.

properties.name: reverse
properties.notes: 0 = forward (the normal downdraft), 1 = reverse. oogje maps 1 to HomeKit clockwise. The vendor app offers Reverse but recommends never using it and running slowly forward in winter instead.

properties.name: speed
properties.notes: The app's seven speeds; 0 stops rotation. aiobafi6 rejects values outside 0-7. Firmware 3.x replaced the legacy firmware's finer steps with these seven.

properties.name: comfort_enabled
properties.notes: Auto Comfort on/off.

properties.name: comfort_ideal_temperature
properties.notes: Hundredths of a degree Celsius on the wire whatever the app displays: 2350 = 23.50 C. The app's own bounds are not established.

properties.name: comfort_min_speed
properties.notes: 0 = no minimum (the app's No Min).

properties.name: comfort_max_speed
properties.notes: 7 = no maximum (the app's No Max).

properties.name: fan_motion_sense
properties.notes: Fan Auto responds to motion. The app requires at least one of Comfort, Motion or a thermostat link to stay enabled while Auto is on.

properties.name: whoosh
properties.notes: Whoosh latches the current speed and varies it around that point (Home Assistant documentation).

properties.name: heat_assist_speed
properties.notes: Bounds are Home Assistant's; aiobafi6 does not validate this field.

properties.name: heat_assist_reverse
properties.notes: Direction used during Heat Assist. Home Assistant does not expose it, and whether the app does is not established.

properties.name: current_rpm
properties.notes: Not pushed on change; re-query for it.

properties.name: eco
properties.notes: oogje: Haiku fans. Capability bit 14 per oogje.

properties.name: fan_occupancy
properties.notes: API version 5+. Clears about 4.5 minutes after the last detection (aiobafi6); Home Assistant says about 5 minutes.

properties.name: light_mode
properties.notes: Acts on the light(s) chosen by field 82 on a fan with both an uplight and a downlight (oogje).

properties.name: light_brightness
properties.notes: The app's brightness percentage. 0 turns the light off (oogje).

properties.name: light_brightness_level
properties.notes: The same brightness as 17 steps. Home Assistant drives this one (level / 16 x 255).

properties.name: light_color_temperature
properties.notes: Kelvin, not mireds. See light_color_presets.

properties.name: light_target
properties.notes: Which light later light commits act on, for fans with both lights. oogje commits it before each light command.

properties.name: standby_led
properties.notes: Sub-fields: 1 colour preset, 2 enabled, 3 percent, 4/5/6 red/green/blue.

properties.name: light_occupancy
properties.notes: API version 5+. Clears about 9.5 minutes after the last detection.

properties.name: temperature
properties.notes: On some models this comes from the Bluetooth remote or wall control, not the fan.

properties.name: humidity
properties.notes: Disputed scaling. aiobafi6 (and so Home Assistant) reads whole percent and treats values outside 0-100 as no sensor; oogje divides by 100. Check against hardware.

properties.name: wifi
properties.notes: Sub-field 1 SSID (aiobafi6); sub-field 2 RSSI in dBm (oogje, hypothesis).

properties.name: beep
properties.notes: The power-on beep the manual says can be turned off in the app.

properties.name: remote_firmware
properties.notes: The paired remote or wall control. Sub-fields 2 version, 3 bootloader, 4 MAC (aiobafi6); oogje reads sub-field 1 as the kind (0 Bluetooth remote, 1 Bluetooth wall control).

properties.name: stats
properties.notes: Sub-field 1 is uptime in minutes (volatile). oogje: 2 total reboots, 3 reboots since power-on, 4 last reboot reason.

properties.name: group
properties.notes: Room/group membership: sub-field 2 uuid, 3 name.

properties.name: uvc_enabled
properties.notes: UV-C uplight option; the manual says it lights only while the fan spins.

query_groups.0: Everything. What aiobafi6 sends on connect and on its timer, and the app's full refresh (reported).
query_groups.3: Firmware, clock and API properties (aiobafi6's name). The vendor app sends this one repeatedly, which makes it the app's keepalive (reported; oogje copies it).
query_groups.5: Schedules (aiobafi6's name). Replies carry query_result field 3.
query_groups.6: Sensors (aiobafi6's name). oogje sends this first on connect and calls it capabilities.
query_groups.7: Exists in the vendor app's query enum (which runs 0-8). Meaning unknown.
query_groups.8: Exists in the vendor app's query enum. Meaning unknown.

test_vectors.description: Generated with an independent standard-library encoder and checked byte for byte against aiobafi6's own serializer. Hex, as sent on the socket.
encoding_recipe: property = varint(field << 3 | 0) || varint(value)   (field 46 -> f0 02; field 48 -> 80 03; field 71 -> b8 04)
commit frame payload = 12 len(A) A, where A = 12 len(B) B and B = 1a len(property) property

vectors.name: query group 3 (the vendor app's timer query)
fan push: speed 3, then temperature 22.40 C (raw 2240)
vectors.notes: The escape case. 2240 encodes as varint c0 11, and the c0 goes out as db dc. Un-escaped: 12 0d | 22 0b | 12 03 f0 02 03 | 12 04 b0 05 c0 11. That is two property sets in one query_result: field 46 = 3, then field 86 = 2240.

baf_i6_api.transport: Plain TCP, port 31415 (the SRV port of _api._tcp). No TLS, no authentication.

remaining_unknowns: The Wi-Fi credential message on the BLE channel. Without it onboarding still needs the vendor app.
The schedule and sleep-mode wire formats. Schedules are stored on the device and fetched with query group 5, but no project decodes them.
Whether the fan applies more than one property per commit. Every known client sends one at a time.
Humidity scaling (aiobafi6 and oogje disagree) and the capability bit for the uplight (sub-field 6 or 11).
The ideal-temperature range the app allows, and the app's own bounds for the motion and return-to-Auto timeouts. The bounds here are Home Assistant's.
What query groups 7 and 8 mean, and the meaning of fields 67 and 109, which oogje logs as 'fan on means auto' and 'light on means auto'.
How the pre-2023 Haiku L 'Wi-Fi' onboarding route works.
Whether a firmware update is prepared by a protobuf message before the HTTP upload on 31416, and what an interrupted update leaves behind. Upload framing is out of scope on purpose.
Whether Matter and the 31415 API run side by side on current smart boards, and from which firmware.
The connection limit, and whether the occasional drops oogje reports are the fan closing idle sockets.
Whether the Turbo6, Mammoth, Bison and Speakeasy model strings in the app's table speak this protocol with the same fields. They are matched by identification but not declared as variants.
Whether the Haiku Switch model string is the Wi-Fi wall control, and what it exposes. It is matched but has no variant or entities.
